title: Γεωργοῦ παῖδες ⟨στασιάζοντες⟩
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 86 (= Perry 53). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« », ⟨ ⟩ for editorial supplements). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.n: στασιάζω is the political word: στάσις is faction, civil strife inside a single city. Used of brothers it makes the household a city at war with itself, and the epimythium closes on the same term.

sentences.t: Ὁ δέ, ὡς πολλὰ παραινῶν οὐκ ἠδύνατο πεῖσαι αὐτοὺς λόγοις μεταβάλλεσθαι, ἔγνω δεῖν διὰ πράγματος τοῦτο πρᾶξαι, καὶ παρῄνεσεν αὐτοῖς ῥάβδων δέσμην κομίσαι.
sentences.tr: Ho de, hōs polla parainōn ouk ēdynato peisai autous logois metaballesthai, egnō dein dia pragmatos touto praxai, kai parēinesen autois rhabdōn desmēn komisai.
sentences.l: And he, since advising many things he was not able to persuade them by words to change, judged it necessary to accomplish this by a deed, and urged them to bring a bundle of rods.
sentences.i: Since for all his advising he could not talk them round, he decided the thing would have to be done by a deed, and told them to fetch a bundle of rods.
sentences.n: ἔγνω δεῖν, 'he judged that it was necessary' — aorist of γιγνώσκω governing an infinitive; the same idiom opens the maidservants' fatal decision in fable 89. λόγοις … διὰ πράγματος, 'by words … by means of a deed', is the hinge the whole fable turns on.

sentences.t: Τῶν δὲ τὸ προσταχθὲν ποιησάντων, τὸ μὲν πρῶτον δοὺς αὐτοῖς ἀθρόας τὰς ῥάβδους ἐκέλευσε κατεάσσειν.
sentences.tr: Tōn de to prostachthen poiēsantōn, to men prōton dous autois athroas tas rhabdous ekeleuse kateassein.
sentences.l: And they having done the thing ordered, first, giving them the rods all in a mass, he bade them break them.
sentences.i: When they had done as they were told, he first handed them the rods all together and told them to break them.
sentences.n: Τῶν δὲ … ποιησάντων is a genitive absolute: the participle's subject is not the subject of the main verb, so the phrase stands outside the sentence's grammar — one of the commonest joints in these fables. τὸ προσταχθέν, aor. pass. participle of προστάσσω made a noun by the article, 'the thing ordered'.

sentences.t: Ἐπειδὴ δὲ κατὰ πᾶν βιαζόμενοι οὐκ ἠδύναντο, ἐκ δευτέρου λύσας τὴν δέσμην, ἀνὰ μίαν αὐτοῖς ῥάβδον ἐδίδου.
sentences.tr: Epeidē de kata pan biazomenoi ouk ēdynanto, ek deuterou lysas tēn desmēn, ana mian autois rhabdon edidou.
sentences.l: But when, forcing it in every way, they were not able, a second time, having undone the bundle, he went on giving them one rod at a time.
sentences.i: But when for all their straining they could not, he undid the bundle a second time and handed them the rods one by one.
sentences.n: ἀνὰ μίαν … ῥάβδον — distributive ἀνά with a numeral, 'one rod at a time'. The imperfect ἐδίδου is durative against the aorists around it: he went on handing them out, one after another.

sentences.t: Τῶν δὲ ῥᾳδίως κατακλώντων, ἔφη· « Ἀτὰρ οὖν καὶ ὑμεῖς, ὦ παῖδες, ἐὰν μὲν ὁμοφρονῆτε, ἀχείρωτοι τοῖς ἐχθροῖς ἔσεσθε· ἐὰν δὲ στασιάζητε, εὐάλωτοι. »
sentences.tr: Tōn de rhāidiōs kataklōntōn, ephē· « Atar oun kai hymeis, ō paides, ean men homophronēte, acheirōtoi tois echthrois esesthe· ean de stasiazēte, eualōtoi. »
sentences.l: And they easily breaking them, he said: « So then you too, my sons, if you are of one mind, will be unmastered by your enemies; but if you quarrel, easy to take. »
sentences.i: And as they snapped them easily, he said: « So then you too, my sons: if you are of one mind, no enemy will master you; but if you fall to quarrelling, you are there for the taking. »
sentences.n: ἀχείρωτοι τοῖς ἐχθροῖς — verbal adjectives in -τος take a dative of the agent, 'not to be mastered by enemies'. In the second limb εὐάλωτοι is left standing alone; ἔσεσθε carries over. Ἀτὰρ οὖν καί is the standard turn from story to application, spoken here by the father himself rather than by the fabulist.

sentences.t: Ὁ λόγος δηλοῖ ὅτι τοσοῦτον ἰσχυροτέρα ἐστὶν ἡ ὁμόνοια ὅσον εὐκαταγώνιστος ἡ στάσις.
sentences.tr: Ho logos dēloi hoti tosouton ischyrotera estin hē homonoia hoson eukatagōnistos hē stasis.
sentences.l: The story shows that concord is stronger by just so much as faction is easy to overcome.
sentences.n: τοσοῦτον … ὅσον, the correlative pair, 'by so much … by as much as'. The second limb repeats no verb. ὁμόνοια and στάσις are the two standing political terms of Greek civic life; the family quarrel closes in the vocabulary of the city.
